title: The 1st (lagna) lord is in a kendra or trikona

text.en: The lord of the 1st (lagna) house sits in a kendra or trikona, which classical texts read as support for health and vitality.
text.impact: Your constitution has good support. You tend to recover well and to keep your energy through demanding stretches.

source.note: Authored from general knowledge of a commonly taught Parashari principle and reviewed by AI at the product owner's direction. No textual citation has been verified; an astrologer may re-review.

review.reviewer: Claude (AI review at the product owner's direction)

title: The 1st (lagna) lord is in the 6th, 8th or 12th house

text.en: The lord of the 1st (lagna) house sits in a dusthana (the 6th, 8th or 12th), which classical texts read as strain on health and vitality.
text.impact: Your body tends to let you know when you overdo things. Regular sleep, meals at fixed times and routine check-ups do more for you than they do for most people.

text.en: The lord of the 1st (lagna) house is exalted, in moolatrikona or in its own sign, and able to give its results fully.
text.impact: A strong constitution. Good stamina and quick recovery are the usual pattern.

title: The 1st (lagna) lord is debilitated

text.en: The lord of the 1st (lagna) house is debilitated, which classical texts read as difficulty with health and vitality, unless the debilitation is cancelled.
text.impact: Energy can run lower than you would like, especially after pushing hard for a long stretch. Building health steadily, through rest, food and exercise you actually enjoy, matters more than any quick fix.

title: The 1st (lagna) lord's debilitation is cancelled

text.en: The lord of the 1st (lagna) house is debilitated, but a recognised condition cancels the debilitation (neecha bhanga).
text.impact: The weakness is cancelled. Frailty earlier in life tends to give way to better health as the years go on.

text.en: The lord of the lagna is combust, too close to the Sun, traditionally read as lower resilience.
text.impact: You may run on empty without noticing it. Pacing yourself, and stopping before you are exhausted, is the useful habit here.

text.impact: Your health responds to how you live, more visibly than it does for most people. Attention to rest, food and movement pays off quickly, and neglect shows up quickly too.

text.impact: This sounds odd but is good news: the tradition reads it as the strength to throw off illness, and to come through competition and opposition intact.

text.impact: It is worth being attentive to your health rather than assuming it looks after itself. Small complaints seen to early rarely become big ones.

text.impact: Your energy tends to come in cycles, with stretches of strain among them. Regular check-ups, and not ignoring symptoms, are the practical answer.

title: The Moon shares a sign with Saturn, Rahu or Ketu
subject: moon

text.en: The Moon, significator of the mind, shares a sign with Saturn, Rahu or Ketu, traditionally read as a tendency to emotional strain; rest and routine help.
text.impact: The mind can carry more than it lets on: worry, broken sleep or low mood coming in phases. Rest, routine, people you can talk to, and professional help when you need it all make a difference.

title: Saturn in the lagna: joints and posture

text.en: Saturn in the lagna is traditionally associated with stiffness in the joints and bones. Regular movement and good posture are worth attention.
text.impact: In practice: stiffness, and aches in the back or joints that come with cold weather or long sitting. Daily movement and attention to posture are what help.

title: Mars in the lagna: heat and minor injuries

text.en: Mars in the lagna is traditionally associated with heat, inflammation and minor cuts or injuries. Avoiding haste helps.
text.impact: In practice: heat in the body, inflammation, and the occasional cut, burn or sporting injury from moving fast. Slowing down at the right moments prevents most of it.

title: The Sun in the 6th, 8th or 12th: energy and eyes

text.en: The Sun in a dusthana is traditionally associated with fluctuating energy and attention to the eyes and heart. Regular check-ups are a sensible habit.
text.impact: In practice: energy that dips, and eyes that tire. Regular check-ups, including eyes and heart, are a sensible habit rather than a cause for worry.

title: Rahu or Ketu in the lagna: seek clear diagnosis

text.en: Rahu or Ketu in the lagna is traditionally associated with complaints that are hard to pin down. A proper medical diagnosis matters more than guesswork.
text.impact: In practice: complaints that are vague or hard to name. The useful response is a proper diagnosis from a doctor rather than guesswork or self-treatment.
